title: Web browsers
blurb: Chrome, Edge, Safari and Firefox: slow, crashing, pop-ups, certificate warnings.

remedies.title: Videos won't play in the browser (black, spinning or no sound)
remedies.why: An extension, hardware acceleration, an old browser, or a site that needs DRM blocks playback.

steps.text: Try a private window (no extensions) and another browser.
Turn off "Use graphics acceleration when available" (Chrome/Edge › Settings › System) and restart the browser.
Update the browser.
For streaming services, check Protected content is allowed in site settings.
Check the tab isn't muted (right-click the tab).

remedies.title: My tabs disappeared after closing the browser
remedies.why: The browser didn't restore the last session, or it was closed in another window.

steps.text: Press Ctrl+Shift+T (⌘+Shift+T) repeatedly to reopen closed tabs and windows.
History › Recently closed shows whole windows to reopen.
Set the browser to continue where you left off: Chrome/Edge › Settings › On startup.
Bookmark important tab groups so they survive crashes.

remedies.title: Bookmarks or favourites disappeared
remedies.why: You're in another profile, the bookmarks bar is hidden, or sync isn't on.

steps.text: Show the bookmarks bar: Ctrl+Shift+B (⌘+Shift+B).
Check the profile picture: bookmarks belong to a profile.
Sign in and turn on sync to bring them back from the cloud.
Moving browsers: Import bookmarks from the other browser in Settings.

remedies.title: "This site is blocked" by my organisation
remedies.why: Your workplace filters some websites for security or policy.

steps.text: Check the address is spelled right (look-alike sites get blocked).
If you need it for work, ask IT to review the site; include the address and why.

remedies.escalate: Only IT can unblock sites on work devices; don't use a VPN to get around it.

remedies.title: Browser fills in old addresses or card details
remedies.why: The browser saved details you've since changed.

steps.text: Chrome/Edge › Settings › Autofill: edit or delete addresses and payment methods.
In a form, highlight the wrong suggestion and press Shift+Delete to remove it.
Safari › Settings › AutoFill › Edit next to each kind.

remedies.title: Website text is too big or too small
remedies.why: The browser remembers a zoom level per site.

steps.text: Press Ctrl+0 (⌘+0) to reset, Ctrl/⌘ + plus or minus to change.
Set a default zoom: Chrome/Edge › Settings › Appearance › Page zoom.

remedies.title: Can't install a browser extension
remedies.why: Your organisation controls extensions, or the extension was removed for safety.

steps.text: Check chrome://management (Edge: edge://management); if it says the browser is managed, IT decides.
Install extensions only from the official stores.

remedies.escalate: Ask IT to approve the extension for work use.

remedies.title: Start the browser fresh (new profile) without losing bookmarks
remedies.why: A damaged profile causes odd problems; a new one with sync brings your things back.

steps.text: Make sure sync is on, or export bookmarks (Bookmarks manager › ⋮ › Export).
Add a new profile (picture at the top › Add), sign in, turn on sync.
Use it for a day; if the problem is gone, remove the old profile.

remedies.title: A site works in Chrome but not Safari
remedies.why: Safari's tracking protection and pop-up blocking can break some sites, and a few sites only test in Chrome.

steps.text: Safari › Settings for This Website: allow Pop-up Windows, turn off content blockers for it.
Safari › Settings › Privacy: try turning off "Prevent cross-site tracking" for a moment (turn it back on after).
Clear that site's data: Settings › Privacy › Manage Website Data.
Use Chrome or Edge for that one site.

remedies.title: A site needs pop-ups but the browser blocks them
remedies.why: Pop-up blockers also stop windows that work sites and payment pages need.

steps.text: Click the blocked pop-up icon in the address bar › Always allow from this site.
Chrome/Edge › Settings › Site permissions › Pop-ups and redirects › Allowed sites.
Safari › Settings for This Website › Pop-up Windows: Allow.
